title: Ephemeral Shadow KV Allocator and Token-Cluster Compaction
creator: Elena Park
description: Background: Continuous batching combined with heterogeneous request profiles leads to high internal fragmentation in the GPU-resident KV cache. Small ephemeral KV entries created by short requests interleave with long-lived conversational entries, leaving holes that are hard to reclaim without expensive stop-the-world compaction. This ticket proposes a two-part approach: (1) an Ephemeral Shadow KV Allocator that segregates short-lived/batch-scoped entries into transient shadow pools to reduce hole-creation in the main pools, and (2) a Token-Cluster Compaction process that incrementally coalesces holes by grouping entries with token-affinity and rewriting hot clusters during low-util windows.
proposal: 1) Ephemeral Shadow KV Allocator: implement a lightweight shadow pool per batcher epoch that holds KV entries for requests below a size/TTL threshold. Shadow pools are allocated from pre-reserved GPU slabs sized by recent short-request histograms. On TTL expiry or when a shadow slab reaches a threshhold, entries are either discarded (if truly ephemeral) or promoted into the main KV pool via an epochal copy that preserves locality.
proposal_continued: 2) Token-Cluster Compaction: collect lightweight access-signatures (token-affinity sketches) sampled during normal serving. Use these signatures to form clusters of entries that are co-accessed. Run background micro-rewrites that migrate clustered entries into contiguous lanes, reclaiming holes without global stop-the-world passes. Compaction is rate-limited by GPU SM availability and workload SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: Live fragmentation metric decreases by >= 30% for workloads with >20% short requests compared to baseline
Overall GPU memory usable capacity increases by >= 10% in representative replay tests
No p99 latency regression > 5% under standard load profiles
Shadow pool promotion path tested with unit and integration tests and covered in CI
Telemetry emitted: shadow_pool_hits, shadow_pool_promotions, token_cluster_size, compaction_rewrite_rate

notes: Initial microbenchmarks show shadow pools reduce hole churn for short chat requests by ~40% in lab traces.
Promotion cost must be amortized; experiments show batching promotions every 100ms yields best trade-off.
Token-cluster sketch uses 128-bit bloom-ish locality signature sampled every N steps to bound overhead.
We need to coordinate with runtime scheduling to avoid compaction interfering with high-priority inference lanes.
risks: Incorrect promotion heuristics could increase copy overhead and raise latency for tail requests
Sketch collisions may produce suboptimal clustering for some languages or tokenizers
Background rewrites could contend with kernel scheduling leading to transient p99 spikes if not properly throttled
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag and canary pool: ENABLE_EPHEMERAL_SHADOW_ALLOCATOR=false by default
Stage 1: internal replay on perf cluster with synthetic mixes (2 weeks)
Stage 2: dedicated canary on low-traffic customer pool (1 week)
Stage 3: monitored gradual rollout with auto-disable threshold tied to p99 latency and compaction_rewrite_rate
Rollback: flip runtime flag off or apply immediate compaction pause policy
telemetry_and_observability: Metrics to emit: shadow_pool_allocs, shadow_pool_frees, shadow_pool_promotions, main_pool_evictions, token_cluster_counts, compaction_latency_ms, compaction_bytes_migrated
Dashboards: new 'KV Allocation' panel in Console under runtime-2.3, per-model breakdown
Alerts: compaction_rewrite_rate > configured_threshold or p99_latency increase > 5% over baseline
integration_notes: Requires minor proto change: include epoch_id in batcher metadata so shadow pools can align with batcher epochs
Must coordinate with KV telemetry team to add access-signature sampling hook
Need to validate with Dedicated autoscaler to ensure reserved slabs are sized correctly for tenant pools
